text:
A rate rise changes what every house is worth without changing the house. From March 2022 to July 2023, the Federal Reserve raised its policy rate from near zero to 5.25–5.5%. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate follows ten-year Treasury yields more closely than it follows Fed announcements. It climbed from roughly 3% to above 7%.

On a $400,000 loan, the monthly payment went from about $1,686 to $2,661. Buyers found that they could borrow more than a third less than before, so the old prices no longer passed their affordability calculations.

Many owners also have loans below 4% and don't want to give them up, so they stay where they are. This "golden handcuffs" effect keeps the number of homes for sale low. Sales slow down before prices fall: US existing-home sales dropped to 4.09 million in 2023, the lowest since 1995.

Credit is what keeps the housing market moving. Higher rates make it scarcer, and demand shrinks as a result.
